name: assembly_patterns
description: Inline assembly memory corruption from failing to update the free memory pointer after manual allocation
question: The source file in `source` contains a Solidity inline assembly block that obtains a memory pointer via `mload(0x40)`, writes data past that pointer using `mstore`, and then continues normal execution (i.e., does not immediately `revert` or `return`) without updating the free memory pointer via a subsequent `mstore(0x40, ...)`, thereby allowing later Solidity-level memory allocations to overwrite the written data and corrupt program state.
criteria: assembly block reads `let ptr := mload(0x40)` to get the current free memory pointer
one or more `mstore(ptr, ...)` or `mstore(add(ptr, ...), ...)` writes beyond the original free memory boundary
no corresponding `mstore(0x40, <new_ptr>)` update after the writes
control flow proceeds to further Solidity code or additional memory allocations after the assembly block, rather than an immediate `revert(...)` or `return(...)` terminating execution
the allocated region is later relied upon (e.g., passed to `keccak256`, `call`, `return`, or read back) after other memory-using operations could have overwritten it
